issues.claim: severity_reason: 'no live page describes the business's services or service area'
issues.problem: Contradicted by the report's own evidence: biondo-contracting.webflow.io is live and describes services (installations, repairs, skylight replacement, flashing, ventilation, siding) and a service area ('Serving Central New Jersey since 1990'). Verified by opening the page today.
issues.fix: Reword to what is true: no page at biondoroofing.com itself describes the services or service area, so the link on the Google profile dead-ends.

issues.claim: founder_md outreach email: 'Your domain is still registered in your name through 2030'
issues.problem: Unsupported. The .com RDAP record is thin and shows no registrant; the report's own data_gaps says registrant identity is not public. The expiry date is confirmed, ownership is not. Telling an owner it is 'in your name' could be wrong (e.g. if a developer or agency holds the account).
issues.fix: Change to: 'the domain is still registered and paid through 7 December 2030, with GoDaddy locks in place' and ask the owner who controls the account.

issues.problem: No cited source supports it and the phone line was not (and could not be) tested. Every source only shows the number as listed. Stated as fact to the business owner.
issues.fix: Say 'the phone number is still listed on your profile and on other directories' or drop the sentence.

issues.claim: domains[1].result: the Webflow page has 'No phone number, address, form or photos of its own'
issues.problem: The page contains a hero photo (jpeg served from its own Webflow site assets). Only the phone/address/form part is correct.
issues.fix: Remove 'or photos of its own'; e.g. 'no phone number, address or form, and one photo'.

issues.claim: after_fix.evidence: 'the profile's 4.9 rating and review volume (172 reviews on Birdeye)'
issues.problem: Conflates two different profiles and ratings. The 4.9 is the Google Business Profile; the 172 reviews belong to the Birdeye profile, which shows 4.7, not 4.9.
issues.fix: Split the sentence: '4.9 on the Google profile; 4.7 from 172 reviews on Birdeye'.

issues.claim: audit_md fix step 4 and fix_steps[3]: update the 'Houzz' link
issues.problem: Houzz is named as one of the places publishing the domain, but the auditor's own caveat says the Houzz profile returned 429 and was never confirmed. Only a search-result summary (which does name biondoroofing.com on a Houzz profile) supports it; I could not open the page either (JS-only/incomplete fetch).
issues.fix: Either mark it as 'if Houzz lists the domain' in audit_md, or drop Houzz from the customer-facing step until the page is confirmed.

issues.claim: fix_steps[3].source_url: https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177 used to back 'edit the website field on the Google Business Profile'
issues.problem: That page is titled 'Guidelines for representing your business on Google' and does not explain editing the website field. The step is fine, the citation does not support it.
issues.fix: Cite the Google help page on editing your Business Profile, or cite the profile URL itself as the thing to be edited.

issues.problem: None of these files are present in the review folder, so the screenshots backing the visual claims (390 px layout, Play-style page, profile panel) cannot be verified.
issues.fix: Save the screenshots alongside rescue.json and re-check the paths before the report is used.
